 ;; Task grounded in rotten (github.com/enajski/rotten), a rot.js roguelike:
 ;; db.cljs world = {[x y] tile}, a dense 30x30 maze grid (generate-maze,

 :levels [{:id :x :type :long}
          {:id :y :type :long}]
 :leaf {:type :object}
 :patterns [{:id :tile :bind [:key :key]
             :doc "point tile read: get-tile, is-walkable?, light-passes?, FOV draw"
             :sites ["db.cljs:56 get-tile" "core.cljs:44 is-walkable?"
                     "core.cljs:200 light-passes?" "core.cljs:285 with-360-fov"]}
            {:id :seen-scan :bind [:scan :scan]
             :doc "full world reduction: display-seen each frame; also the filter of get-random-empty-location"
             :sites ["core.cljs:296 display-seen" "core.cljs:49 get-random-empty-location"]}]
 ;; Baseline: the persistent nested map the game actually uses.
 :orders [{:perm [0 1] :format :hash}]
 ;; Per frame: FOV radius 10 ~ 314 cells x ~3 tile reads ~ 900 point reads,
 ;; plus one full-world scan (display-seen). A* and random-location add
 ;; occasional points/scans between frames; the frame mix dominates.
 :workload {:fanout [30 30]
            :fill [1.0 1.0]
            :seed 7

 :notes "rotten case study: dense 30x30 grid, point-dominated render loop.
         Vector keys [x y] modeled as two long levels; tile maps as object leaves.
         Weights approximate one rendered frame (900 FOV/path point reads : 1 full scan)."}

(defn display-seen [world]
  (doseq [[[x y] tile] world]
    (when (:tile/seen? tile)
      (draw-tile x y tile)
      (draw-seen-overlay x y))))

(defn with-360-fov [origin-x origin-y range world]
  (.compute FOVHandler origin-x origin-y range
            (fn [x y r _visibility]
              (when (db/get-tile x y)
                (db/mark-tile-as-seen x y)
                (draw-tile x y (get world [x y]))
                (doseq [entity (db/get-tile-entities x y)]
                  (draw-entity x y entity))))))
